lines.text: Quick round: why does a tiny favor make you feel like you owe someone?
Psychologists call it the rule of reciprocity.
In one study, a stranger brought people a Coke they never asked for.
Later, he asked them to buy raffle tickets.
Compared with people who got nothing, those with the free Coke bought about twice as many tickets.
The favor worked even when they didn't like him much.
So when a freebie feels like a debt, ask who set the price.

post.title: Why a Free Gift Makes You Feel Like You Owe #shorts
post.description: A small favor creates a big sense of debt. In Regan (1971), people who got an unrequested Coke from a stranger later bought about twice as many raffle tickets from him, whether or not they liked him. That's the rule of reciprocity. #psychology #persuasion #socialpsychology
